predecessors.name: Greek city-states (independent poleis)
predecessors.text: Dyme, Patrae, Pharae and Tritaea in western Achaea, which 'revived' the league in 281/0

successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: the whole Peloponnese and Megaris, 'grouped into the Roman province of Macedonia' after Corinth was razed and 'the League' dissolved in 146

ledger.x: 280: 'The regional Achaean League was revived in 281/0 BC by the communities of Dyme, Patrae, Pharae, and Tritaea'.

275: 'Around the year 275 BC, the people expelled the Macedonian garrison and the city joined the new Achaean League'; 'joined in 275 by Aegium, which controlled the important sanctuary of Zeus Homarios'.
275: Aegium (38.251 N, 22.081 E) 'became the Achaean assembly place' and 'remained their capital until the Roman conquest in 146 BC'.
251: Aratus 'overthrew the tyranny in his native city and brought it into the Achaean League'; the first non-Achaean member.
243: Aratus 'captured Corinth and the fortress of Acrocorinth in 243 BC in a daring night attack' from the Macedonian garrison; 'After its capture by Aratus, Corinth also joined the Achaean League'.
243 ('shortly afterwards'): Corinth 'was followed shortly afterwards by Megara, Troezen, and Epidaurus'.
235: Lydiades, tyrant of Megalopolis, 'decided to give up his power by joining the Achaean League' ('That year', 235); 'Corinth was followed by Megalopolis in 235 BC and Argos in 229 BC'.
Soon after 235 (undated: 'Orchomenus and Mantinea soon followed suit'): the eastern Arcadian cities.
229: 'Argos in 229 BC'; 'Aristomachus of Argos also abandoned the Macedonian alliance and joined the Achaean League'.
229/228 to 222: the Cleomenean War (infobox 'Sparta, Elis vs.
226: 'In 226 BC, the citizens of Mantinea appealed to Cleomenes to expel the Achaean garrison from the city'; he 'removed the garrison that night'.

225 (year from the narrative): Cleomenes took Argos during the Nemean Games, the Argives 'accepted a garrison, delivered twenty hostages to Cleomenes and became Spartan allies'; 'Cleonae, Phlius, Hermione, Troezen, and Epidaurus surrendered to him', 'The Corinthians did surrender the city to Cleomenes', who 'besieged…
224: 'Aratus agreed to give Acrocorinth to Antigonus in return for his support'; 'Cleomenes gave up the Isthmus and Corinth fell to Antigonus'.
224: 'The Argives revolted against Cleomenes, and the Achaean reinforcements took the whole city except the citadel'; with Antigonus's advance the Acte cities returned.
223: 'Megara deserted the Achaean League and joined the Boeotian Confederacy', cut off by Macedonian Corinth.
Summer 222: Sellasia, 'Decisive Macedonian-Achaean victory'; 'Antigonus became the first non-Spartan general to occupy Sparta' and 'did not force Sparta to join the League'.

Spring 220 to 217: Aetolian troops 'pillaged the countryside of several Achaean cities, namely Patras and Pharae' and burned 'the Arcadian city of Cynaetha'; 'In the summer of 219 BC Sparta attacked Achaea from the south'.
Winter 219/218: Philip V 'stormed the city of Psophis and handed it over to his Achaean ally Aratus the Younger'; 'The same procedure was used at Lasion'.
217: the Peace of Naupactus, 'every side should maintain what it currently possessed'.

Winter 198/197: Argos went over to Philip V when the league 'voted to join the anti-Macedonian alliance' at Sicyon (198), and 'Philip handed Argos to Nabis, who then engineered a revolution there and agreed at Mycenae to stop attacking the Achaeans'.
197: 'Corinth rejoined' (membership list); 'The Romans reportedly offered the city of Corinth to the League as an inducement'.
197-194: 'Roman garrisons remained in Corinth, Chalcis, and Demetrias until 194 BC' (rule 4 hatch over the Achaean colour).
195: 'Flamininus ordered Nabis to give Argos back to the Achaeans, or face war with Rome'; after the Spartan defeat 'Nabis was forced to surrender both Argos and the port of Gytheum'.
194: Flamininus withdraws the garrisons of Corinth, Chalcis and Demetrias.
192: Nabis 'was assassinated in 192 BC by the Aetolian League'; afterwards Philopoemen 'compelled the Spartans to join the Achaean League'.
191: Messene and Messenia enter the league.

191: Hypana in Elis is listed as a later member and Elis itself is named as a hostile independent state, not a member; the Roman-Seleucid War page lists Elis on the Seleucid side. greek-city-states /ledger/68 carries the matching 191 loss of 'Messene and Elis' with the rest…
183: 'Dinocrates, who strongly opposed Philopoemen, encouraged Messene to revolt against the League'; Philopoemen was captured and killed there (183 or 182).
182: 'On hearing of his death, the members of the Achaean League joined forces to capture Messene' (Lycortas).
150: 'hostilities between Sparta and the League flared up again'; in 147 the Roman envoy Orestes 'tried to announce the forced reduction of the Achaean League to its original, narrow grouping'.
146: the Roman settlement ends the dispute with the league's dissolution.

146: Metellus 'decisively defeated' Critolaos 'at the Battle of Scarpheia'; Diaeus's army was routed at Corinth, and the Romans 'destroyed the city'; 'the Greek states were grouped into the Roman province of Macedonia'.
146: the Romans 'razed Corinth and dissolved the League'; 'all leagues and other political entities were dissolved'.

wars.name: Cleomenean War
wars.outcome: 'Achaean and Macedonian victory'; 'Acrocorinth, Corinth, Heraea, and Orchomenus to Macedon'; Cleomenes fled to Egypt.

wars.name: Social War (220-217)
wars.outcome: 'Macedonian and Achaean victory'; 'Psophis and Lasion to Achaea'.

wars.name: First Macedonian War
wars.outcome: 'stalemate and Peace of Phoenice' (205); no ground changed hands for the league.

wars.name: Second Macedonian War (Achaean participation)
wars.outcome: 'Roman coalition victory'; Corinth to the league (197), Argos to Nabis until 195.

wars.name: War against Nabis
wars.outcome: Nabis 'forced to surrender both Argos and the port of Gytheum'.

wars.name: Roman-Seleucid War
wars.outcome: Roman coalition victory: Antiochus 'ceded all of his territories beyond the Taurus Mountains to Roman allies'; for the league, Messene and Elis end up inside it, undated (191 bridge).

wars.name: Achaean War
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory'; 'Roman annexation of mainland Greece'; the league dissolved.

certainty.note: A league of cities: each member's chora is approximated by a radius; accession years firm for the named cities, unknown for the small ones.
Membership changed yearly in the Cleomenean, Social and Macedonian wars; the Argolid, Corinth and Arcadia carry blends and hatches.
The whole Peloponnese and Megaris; the coastline is the border except toward Megara-Boeotia.
